paper_summary: Hungarian-language conference paper (XXII. Fiatal Muszakiak Tudomanyos Ulesszaka, 2017) on fracture-mechanics testing of ceramic hollow sphere filled aluminium matrix syntactic foams. Al99.5 and AlSi12 matrices were infiltrated around Hollomet GmbH Globocer mixed-oxide ceramic hollow spheres (1450+/-83 um diameter, 58+/-5 um wall) by inert-gas (Ar) pressure-assisted liquid-phase infiltration, and notched specimens (W = 25 mm, B = W/2, S = 4W, a = 12 mm, notch radius 0.25 mm, not pre-fatigued, 4 specimens per matrix) were tested in three-point bending with force vs crack-opening recorded. Mean FQ was 483+/-128 N (Al99.5) and 711+/-126 N (AlSi12), giving KQ = 115+/-30 and 165+/-31 N/mm^3/2; fracture surfaces showed 63/16/21 % intact/broken/pulled-out spheres for Al99.5 versus 27/70/3 % for AlSi12, attributed to the different sphere-matrix bonding.

structure.microstructure_notes: Sphere wall thickness 58+/-5 um on a 1450+/-83 um diameter sphere. On the fracture surfaces of the Al99.5 matrix samples 63 % of the hollow spheres were intact, 16 % broken and 21 % pulled out (Table 4); the crack propagates mainly through the matrix next to the spheres and only occasionally through them, and the crack plane sometimes departs markedly from the notch plane.

extraction_notes: Four-page Hungarian conference paper read in full (including the [TABLE] blocks). (1) The only quantitative mechanical results are fracture-mechanics quantities: mean FQ = 483+/-128 N and KQ = 115+/-30 N/mm^3/2 for Al99.5, FQ = 711+/-126 N and KQ = 165+/-31 N/mm^3/2 for AlSi12 (Table 5). The schema has no fracture-toughness or force field, so no properties field was filled; the values are preserved here. For reference, 115 N/mm^3/2 = 3.64 MPa*m^0.5 and 165 N/mm^3/2 = 5.22 MPa*m^0.5, but no conversion was written into the record since there is no matching field. The authors explicitly caution these KQ values are not yet valid material constants (KIC) - further measurements are needed. (2) No density, no filler volume/weight fraction, no modulus, strength, strain or energy-absorption values are reported anywhere in the paper, so all Properties and Structure numeric fields are null. (3) particle_wall_thickness_ratio was derived from the reported geometry in Table 3: outer radius 1450/2 = 725 um, wall 58 um, so eta = inner/outer = (725-58)/725 = 0.92. This is derived, not stated verbatim. Diameter uncertainty +/-83 um and wall +/-5 um are not representable in the schema. (4) The intact/broken/pulled-out sphere percentages of Table 4 are counts on the post-test fracture surface, not particles broken during processing, so they were recorded in microstructure_notes rather than in structure.particle_breakage_fraction (whose definition is breakage during processing). (5) Figures 4 and 5 show force vs crack-opening curves only; no numeric values can be read from them. (6) Test temperature (room temperature is implied but never stated) and loading rate/strain rate are not given, so both are null. (7) Evidence quotes are transliterated to ASCII from the Hungarian original (accents removed) but are otherwise verbatim; table quotes are reflowed from the pipe-delimited [TABLE] blocks.
